title: MessagePack: dissect more types+other improvements
description:
Add support for unhandled msgpack data formats:

* `map 16` and `map 32` (expand from `fixmap` support)
* `ext 8`/`ext 16`/`ext 32` (expand from `fixext` support)
* `bin 8`/`bin 16`/`bin 32` (replicate from string type support)

Add a `range_string` lookup for describing the format byte. Create a
tree entry for the format byte in more places. Remove the `value_string`
that was used for this purpose but only on extension types.

Correctly handle negative `fixint`s by representing them as negative
numbers.

Create separate fields (with the same name) for handling the different
sizes of length field used in strings (and by extension, binary
strings).

Fix an inconsistency in string-type handling that falsely stated
`fixstr`s had a length of 1 byte.

Fix a logic error in map and array handling which treated the number of
elements in the structure as being the number of bytes used to represent
the number of elements.

Replace `tvb_get_ptr()`+`bytes_to_hexstr()` with `tvb_bytes_to_str()` in
extension-type handling.

Change field type for `float 32` from `FT_STRING` to `FT_FLOAT`. Create
separate field for `float 64` as `FT_DOUBLE`.

Change some of the generated labels for consistency, and use them more
consistently.

Possible future enhancements:

* More detailed breakdown of types and lengths (need to consult e.g.
  `packet-protobuf.c` for precedent)
* Dissector table for positive extension types
* Handle extension type -1 (timestamps)
* Expert info on other negative (and thus reserved) extension types
* More graceful handling of the "never used"/deprecated `0xc1` type
* More hardening in general

For testing I generated
<https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/wikis/uploads/ecaf7e0e2555d472607ea4c7323e24a5/msgpack-generated.pcap>

notes.body: I believe it's possible for a (probably contrived) packet to contain a type that isn't in this list.  If that's the case, that's not a "dissector logic fault" and shouldn't use DISSECTOR_ASSERT macros.  That sounds like a case for expert info.

`dissect_msgpack_map()` only gets called when the type byte matches one of these three type situations (see where `dissect_msgpack_object()` calls it). I put this assert here to show that it would be an unexpected behaviour. I'm open to other approaches, but I don't think an expert info is appropriate in this case.
Based on your recommendation to remove the assert in `dissect_msgpack_bin()` I'll just remove the assert here too.

Sorry, but still trying to learn gitlab.  I'm a little surprised the pipeline passed with some of the endian issues noted.  Some of the other comments are more about style.

toos/fix-encoding-args.pl is the check that I though might detect incompatible flags, but I don't believe it actually looks up the type of the hf item to make sure the given flags in the call are plausible.

tools/check_typed_item_calls.py does parse both the hf items and and various API calls - presently it only looks for encoding args that look sane, but doesn't constrain them by the hf item being added.

It could do this, but it may not be practical to make this more than a warning.  It does very simple substitutions from preprocessor symbols or enum values, but there are always cases where some other expression appears that it won't fully understand.

The good/bad thing is that ENC_NA == ENC_BIG_ENDIAN == 0

I can/will add this check to check_typed_item_calls.py

Changes in 318269bf:

* Removed all `DISSECTOR_ASSERT_NOT_REACHED()`
* Removed the fields for holding 8 or 16 bit length values, use the 32 bit length field for them all
* Use `ENC_BIG_ENDIAN` for all multi-byte number fields
* Use `ENC_UTF_8` for MsgPack strings since the spec says they're UTF-8
* Renamed some variables in `dissect_msgpack_ext()` to be consistent with names in other functions
* Added a field to show/dissect the length of an `ext` item
* Reduced `lensize` to a `uint8_t` since it's counting a number of bytes which will never be more than 4
